notes: Mapped rules name a direct bounded C# regression or differential control; they do not promote the surrounding Python file or feature family.
Explicit exclusions are limited to DL2, deferred custom-model or CRIG authoring, intentionally unsupported legacy projects, and Python implementation or packaging surfaces.
The final pending rule is deliberately conservative. A test is pending whenever the reviewed rules cannot justify mapped or excluded status.
A newly collected node ID remains unclassified until the exact checked manifest is deliberately regenerated and reviewed, even when a broad rule could assign it pending status.

rules.rationale: The C# animation decoder uses a bounded binary-reader profile that retains the skeleton, authoritative Pose::BindPose matrices, stacks, and curves while excluding model topology payloads. The same installed 11-file compatibility corpus is pinned by exact identity and checks rig, take, frame-count, changing-curve, and skipped-topology behavior without copying those FBXs into the repository; an unavailable corpus is reported as skipped rather than passed.
The cross-language semantic oracle and C# evaluator compare all six FBX Euler orders.
C# directly verifies arbitrary layer-name curve isolation, selected nonzero sample ticks, one-layer enforcement, stack-local malformed-curve diagnostics, and unique-changing-take selection.
C# directly covers declared, fractional, custom, and key-spacing fallback timing.

The bounded C# facial adapter reads selected scalar DeformPercent animation without model topology, preserves the declared source rate and exact selected tick span when sampling at another rational rate, and derives a facial-only span with a low-confidence key-spacing fallback when no declared mode is available.
The C# codec and checked Python byte oracle cover direct and second-order packed values.
C# has a strict readable multipage writer regression.
C# directly matches the requested packed-frame prefix, the strict 61-frame one-page layout, and rejection of a physically oversized payload that still declares one page.
The C# theory checks the same five rotation, translation, rotation-translation, scale, and full-TRS ownership masks against target-bind values.
C# directly evaluates rest-relative helpers against distinct target binds, preserves target translation and scale for rotation-delta transfer, and fails closed on a non-finite helper result.

C# directly proves repeated helper evaluation is deterministic, unmapped helpers remain at target bind, body plus helper fan-out is reported, exact helper identities receive conservative profile policies, and ambiguous normalized helper sources fail closed.
C# accepts one source driving a body row plus multiple helper overrides and proves those helper overrides do not change exact base identity or hierarchy compatibility.
C# directly decodes local/reference/global compact hierarchy matrices and bind-space bounds.
The semantic oracle and C# authoring policy compare all three DL1 root ownership modes.
The direct C# builder and semantic oracle cover deterministic weighted many-source-to-one TX scalar consolidation and verify the resulting ANM2 through the production decoder.

The C# mimic builder reports active unmapped sources rather than inventing bindings and its bounded source scan applies percent normalization only to percent-scale FBX exports while leaving normalized values unchanged.

The embedded C# Common46 profile is bounded, declarative, and descriptor-unique; conservative auto-mapping supports reviewed consolidation and blink companions, and canonical schema-1 round trips preserve unresolved descriptor semantics without guessing.
C# creates, extracts, appends, and atomically writes the bounded animation-library RP6L layout; the semantic oracle compares one exact canonical container.
The C# domain exposes and evaluates the same three DL1 root modes.

The installed Blender gate validates an armature-only bind pose, animation actions, retail mesh, and strict reopened FBX handoff. It does not claim the separate Python FBX-to-ANM2 rebuild and value comparison.
The first C# release is Dying Light 1 only and contains no DL2 code paths, assets, UI, or project fields.
These suites validate DL2 advanced bridge inventories, policies, or private DL2 fixtures.
These parameter or mixed-file nodes are specifically DL2 behavior inside otherwise broader suites.
The remaining private export-first controls use the DL2 player rig, DL2 policy, or private DL2 FPP animation artifacts and are outside the DL1-only first release.
Both exact-source-superset nodes hardcode reference/dl2/player_skeleton.crig and assert its DL2-specific inventory; they contain no DL1 control.
Both nodes load reference/dl2/player_skeleton.crig and assert that DL2 target hierarchy; they are outside the DL1-only first release even though C# has a separate DL1 compatibility regression.
CRIG creation/import/editing, custom-model authoring, and the experimental Models workspace are explicitly deferred from the DL1 first release.
The C# app uses a fresh schema-1 dl-reanimated-csharp-project format and intentionally refuses legacy schema-1 through schema-10 projects without migration or modification.

This node persists Python schema extension dictionaries and a legacy per-animation root-motion override. The C# app intentionally uses a fresh schema-1 dl-reanimated-csharp-project document and does not claim legacy extension round-trip compatibility.
These regressions preserve an obsolete Python 0.5.0 engine/project compatibility mode rather than the fresh C# project and authoritative pipeline contract.
These nodes inspect Python source, Qt patch markers, Python launchers, or the legacy Python package surface rather than user-visible C# behavior.
This node directly exercises the private Python _copy_mapping_state implementation and its deepcopy/row-enabled semantics. The immutable C# document pipeline has no equivalent builder-copy surface.
The C# retail path derives RigDefinition dynamically from DL1 meshes; custom SMD/CRIG target authoring is deferred.
The temporary PySide work-in-progress notice and its QSettings lifecycle are not part of the supported C# application contract.
CRIG creation and import are explicitly deferred.
These nodes exercise the deferred Models workspace and generated CRIG handoff.

The public C# codec directly covers deterministic atomic sidecar writing, canonical UTF-8 output, SHA-256 and frame-count gating, old and optional schema-1 fields, strict scalar/list validation including booleans and huge numeric literals, one nonfatal advisory per rejected sidecar, and provenance-driven reverse-export rates.

The shared Blender-independent C# resampler directly preserves duration and exact endpoints, maps 381 samples at 30 fps to 305 at 24 fps, maintains shortest-hemisphere quaternion continuity, and keeps a single-frame clip singular; the Blender handoff consumes the same plan.

The bounded C# DL1 sampler-v1 controls compare cached bulk output bit-for-bit with random-access decoding on the stock infected-turn clip, decode each synthetic DL1 packed slot once while retaining explicitly selected descriptor order, reject ambiguous or absent selections and oversized output, and cancel from inside active decode work. The latter two Python nodes use a DL2 payload only to exercise target-neutral caching, selection, and cancellation behavior; the C# mapping deliberately covers those behaviors on DL1 data without adding a DL2 codec path.

The direct C# authoring-policy regression animates both a parent and its selected pelvis child, removes world-up heading in InPlace mode, reconstructs a finite child-local transform, preserves the animated parent, restores bind-global position, and leaves the DL1 motion helper at identity.

The C# end-to-end body import control encodes and decodes 257 DL1 sampler-v1 poses across 720 degrees, proves every aligned quaternion remains rotation-equivalent to the scalar Cayley conversion, and requires every adjacent imported key to stay in the same quaternion hemisphere.

The C# Blender handoff now constructs and consumes distinct ordered descriptor selections: the Action pass contains retail-rig tracks plus the motion accumulator, while unresolved tracks are decoded in a separate original-cadence sidecar pass before the Action materialization. Direct service coverage reopens the committed sidecar and verifies its exact descriptor, frame, cadence, and transform values without synthesizing a bone. The Python node uses a DL2 clip to exercise this target-neutral memory policy; the C# evidence locks it on the DL1-only handoff.

The embedded C# handoff helper is directly inspected under test: it never calls per-key keyframe_insert, fills FCurve coordinates with foreach_set, performs exactly one dependency-graph update, disables all-bone and forced endpoint baking, and links the one armature object exactly once. The C# helper uses real retail bones rather than the Python helper object's implementation-specific variable name.

The C# Blender service regression runs active and static DL1 motion-accumulator clips through the actual staged Action/sidecar workflow. Active +2 X motion is baked into the unique retail Root while the original helper samples remain in the committed sidecar; a present but static helper leaves the Root unchanged and is reported as not baked.

The strict C# writer/reader control creates a 2,210-frame DL1 payload with multiple physical 64 KiB pages, bulk-decodes it, and compares random-access versus cached frame values immediately before and after the first page transition and at the final frame.

These exact parameter/fixture nodes load the DL2 far-jump ANM2, the DL2 advanced player CRIG, or a generated 3,343-frame DL2 acceptance artifact. The DL1-first C# reader deliberately rejects the DL2 header and has no DL2 asset or rig path.

This mixed node mutates the legacy Python project from DL1 into a built-in DL2 profile and then into a custom CRIG target. The C# release uses a distinct non-migrating DL1-only project format; DL2 and custom-model/CRIG target authoring are both explicitly deferred.
Applicable ANM2, reverse conversion, provenance, sparse decode, or automatic-root behavior lacks a direct reviewed C# node mapping.
Applicable FBX evaluation, stack, timebase, wrapper, hierarchy, or rejection behavior lacks a direct reviewed C# node mapping.
Applicable Blender/helper round-trip behavior is not covered by the bounded installed C# handoff mapping above.
Applicable broad mapping, helper, source-analysis, profile, or solver behavior is not yet directly mapped to a reviewed C# regression.
Applicable mimic mapping/profile behavior is outside the bounded consolidated scalar and project controls above.
Applicable CLI, script-target, generated-candidate, or release-smoke behavior lacks a direct reviewed C# node mapping.
The behavior remains relevant, but no direct reviewed WPF regression mapping has been recorded for this Python node.
Applicable DL1 private-corpus behavior has not been reproduced by a redistributable C# control or locked installed validation row.
No narrower reviewed rule justifies mapped or explicitly excluded status; pending is the fail-safe classification.
